video_title: Why Circuit Breakers Exist: Contain Failure, Don't Fix It
core_insight: A circuit breaker protects the caller’s finite resources by stopping calls to a failing downstream, trading a controlled fast failure for an uncontrolled slow death from cascading failure.

scenes.voice: Why do healthy services go down because another service is slow? The answer is cascading failure.
scenes.visual: Two services A and B. Arrows from A to B. B slows, A's threads pile up.
scenes.on_screen_text: Healthy service dies from a slow dependency

scenes.voice: Service A calls Service B. B starts erroring or slowing. Without protection, A keeps sending requests. Threads block, connection pools fill, latency rises.
scenes.visual: Thread pool bar filling up in A while requests wait on B. Latency graph climbing.
scenes.on_screen_text: Threads block. Pools fill. Latency amplifies

scenes.voice: Timeouts help once, but repeated calls still pile up. Retries make it worse. The real constraint is A's finite threads and latency budget.
scenes.visual: Timeout icon then retry storm arrows looping back to failing B.
scenes.on_screen_text: Timeouts aren't enough. Retries worsen overload

scenes.voice: Think of an electrical breaker. It stops current to prevent fire. A software circuit breaker stops calls to prevent resource exhaustion.
scenes.visual: Electrical breaker switch next to software breaker diagram.

scenes.voice: It has three states. Closed lets calls through and counts failures. Open rejects calls immediately, giving B time to recover and protecting A. Half-Open probes with limited traffic to test recovery.
scenes.visual: State diagram animating Closed → Open → Half-Open → Closed.
scenes.mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Closed
    Closed --> Open: failure threshold breached
    Open --> HalfOpen: after timeout
    HalfOpen --> Closed: probe succeeds
    HalfOpen --> Open: probe fails

scenes.voice: Order service to Payment gateway. Error rate hits 70%. Breaker opens for 30 seconds. New orders fail fast with a fallback to queue for async retry. Order stays responsive.
scenes.visual: Order → Payment flow. Breaker opens, traffic diverted to fallback queue.

scenes.voice: Circuit breakers don't fix B. They contain failure in A. You trade availability of the dependency for availability of yourself. Tune thresholds carefully, and always pair with a meaningful fallback and observability.
scenes.visual: Scale balancing caller health vs downstream availability.
scenes.on_screen_text: Contain failure. Fail fast on purpose.

mental_model: Treat a downstream call as a resource you can exhaust. A circuit breaker is a fuse for your own threads and latency budget: trip early, recover gradually, and never let a slow neighbor take you down.
final_takeaway: Circuit breakers buy time for recovery by failing fast. They protect the caller, not heal the callee.
